findings.note: Mariner/navigator are both nautical professions and compass/chart are both navigation instruments, so both halves share the 'two items of the same kind' relation. Both halves read as: "two kindred sailor roles (co-hyponyms)" and "two kindred navigation tools (co-hyponyms)".

Lighthouse/ship are both whole structures and lantern room/hull are both structural parts, so both halves share the 'two items of the same kind' relation. Both halves read as: "two kindred large structures (co-hyponyms)" and "two kindred structural parts (co-hyponyms)".

Both halves read as 'keeper responsible for a given signal,' giving a coherent worker-device relation on each side. Both halves read as: "worker who tends a device (keeper tends beacon)" and "worker who tends a device (keeper tends foghorn)".

Swapping the assignment still gives a consistent worker-device relation on both sides since no fixed convention dictates which keeper runs which signal. Both halves read as: "worker who tends a device (keeper tends foghorn)" and "worker who tends a device (keeper tends beacon)".

Dusk and ebb both mark the beginning of their cycles while dawn and flood both mark the end, so both halves share the same 'position in cycle' relation. Both halves read as: "start-of-cycle pairing (dusk/ebb)" and "end-of-cycle pairing (dawn/flood)".

Four sets have cross-reading or order-ambiguity defects flagged by the adversarial solver and integrity checker: set-agent-instrument and set-object-component both admit an unintended 'two co-hyponyms vs two co-hyponyms' reading; set-coordinates has no fixed axis and is order-symmetric with no directional anchor; set-before-after is reversible and the label oversells direction. All fixes stay within the lighthouse-keeper world.
- set-agent-instrument: Mariner/navigator read as two kindred sailor roles and compass/chart as two kindred tools, so the set also validates as 'co-hyponym : co-hyponym' instead of strictly 'worker : their tool.'

  Or: Alternatively replace 'chart' with a tool less tied to 'navigator' specifically, e.g. 'navigator : sextant', to weaken the compass/chart co-hyponym reading
  Or: Or swap 'mariner' for a clearly different kind of worker, e.g. 'lamplighter : wick trimmer', so left-side words are not both sailor titles
- set-object-component: Lighthouse/ship both read as 'whole structures' and lantern room/hull both read as 'structural parts,' so the set also validates as 'structure : structure :: part : part.'
  Try: Replace 'ship' and 'hull' with a non-vessel structure from the same subject, e.g. 'pier : pilings', so the whole-pair no longer reads as two kindred large vessels/structures
  Or: Keep 'lighthouse : lantern room' and change the second pair to 'keeper's cottage : chimney', keeping part-whole necessity but removing the structure/structure co-hyponym pull
  Or: Swap 'lantern room' for a part unique to lighthouses with no ship analog, e.g. 'lighthouse : gallery rail', paired with 'ship : rudder'
- set-coordinates: Set fails on two fronts: (1) principal/assistant keeper is a human-partner pairing while beacon/foghorn is a tool pairing — mismatched grain; (2) the set is fully order-symmetric with no fixed axis, like ram:ewe needing a sex axis, but here nothing fixes which keeper or which signal comes first.

  Or: Alternatively replace 'beacon : foghorn' with a second human-partner pair sharing the same axis as principal/assistant keeper, e.g. 'head keeper : relief keeper' (seniority axis matching principal/assistant)
  Or: If keeping beacon/foghorn, change label and explanation to lock an axis (e.g. 'warns by sight' vs 'warns by sound') and replace principal/assistant keeper with a pair on that same sight/sound axis rather than a seniority axis
- set-before-after: Both pairs are fully reversible (dawn→dusk and flood→ebb work as well as the stated direction), so 'start and end of one span' oversells a directionality the words don't carry; the set also cross-reads as 'start-of-cycle : end-of-cycle' matched across both pairs rather than within each.
